The *Aggi Sutta* ("Fire", Iti 93; It 3.44, PTS It 92) is a discourse in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The discourse expounds the teaching on the three metaphorical "fires": the fire of passion (*rāga*), the fire of aversion (*dosa*), and the fire of delusion (*moha*) [SuttaCentral]. On SuttaCentral, seventeen translations across fifteen languages are indexed, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

No curated parallels in other canonical collections are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. It also shares passages with the *Magga Saṁyutta* of the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 45; 5 matches, 453 characters, notably §2.1–2.4 matching SN 45.168.1.1–168.1.4) and shows formulaic overlap with several other discourses in the *Itivuttaka*, such as Iti 90, Iti 63, Iti 92, Iti 75, Iti 56, Iti 88, and Iti 57 [DharmaNexus].
